definition: The great ash tree whose branches and roots hold the nine worlds together. Its name is often translated as 'Odin's horse'.
The home of the gods, connected to Midgard by the rainbow bridge Bifröst. It is one of the nine worlds.
The middle world and the realm of humans, surrounded by the sea and encircled by the world serpent.
The land of the giants, one of the nine worlds and the usual home of the gods' rivals.
A giant, a member of the race that often opposed the gods. Some giants are monstrous, while others are wise or helpful.
The foretold end of the world, when the gods and their enemies fight and the earth is destroyed and then reborn.
One of the female figures who choose the slain on the battlefield and bring half of them to Valhalla to serve Odin.
The slain warriors who feast and train in Valhalla until Ragnarök, when they will fight alongside Odin.
A letter of the Germanic writing system, and also a sign used in magic. Odin is said to have won the runes through suffering.
The idea of fate or destiny, often pictured as a web woven by the Norns. The Old Norse term is urðr, and even the gods cannot escape it.
